title: For Loops
bullets: Use start, stop and step values.
Process the items in a string or list.

title: Iteration Structures
paragraphs: An iteration structure repeats a block of code.
Each repetition is called an iteration.
Loops are useful when a task needs to happen more than once.
Python provides for loops and while loops. This lesson focuses on for loops.

title: How a for Loop Works
paragraphs: A for loop processes one value at a time from an iterable.
An iterable provides values that a loop can visit. Strings, lists and ranges are examples.
Python assigns the next value to the loop variable. It then runs the indented block.
The loop finishes when there are no values left.

title: Repeating a Set Number of Times
paragraphs: Use range(5) to repeat the block five times.
The indented print runs once during each iteration.
The loop variable _ receives each value. The underscore signals that this example does not use the value.

title: Using Range Values
paragraphs: The loop variable stores the current value.
range(5) provides 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. It starts at 0. It excludes 5.
Here, number is displayed during each iteration.

title: Choosing a Start and Stop
paragraphs: range(start, stop) lets you choose the first value.
The start value is included. The stop value is excluded.
range(5, 10) provides the values 5 through 9.

title: Choosing a Step Size
paragraphs: range(start, stop, step) controls how the value changes.
The default step is 1. Here, the step is 5.
range(0, 21, 5) provides 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. The stop value is still excluded.

title: Counting Backwards
paragraphs: A negative step makes the values decrease.
range(5, 0, -1) provides 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1. It excludes 0.
The step must move toward the stop value. A step of 0 is invalid.

title: Looping Over a String
paragraphs: A string can be visited one character at a time.
The loop variable character stores the current character.
The print instruction displays that character. A descriptive variable name makes its purpose clear.

title: Looping Over a List
paragraphs: A for loop can visit the items in a list directly. Tuples can also be used.
The variable fruit stores the current item. This pattern does not provide its index.
The items are visited in their stored order.

title: Checking Each Item
paragraphs: A condition can be checked during each iteration.
Here, the if statement checks the current grade.
Only grades of 80 or higher are displayed. The loop still visits every grade.

title: Processing Each Item
paragraphs: The same operation can be applied to each item.
Here, upper() creates an uppercase version of the current name.
That version is displayed. The original list is unchanged.

title: Wrap Up
bullets: An iteration is one repetition of a loop.
A for loop processes one value at a time.
Use range to generate integer values. Its stop value is excluded.
Choose a negative step to count backwards.
Visit strings and lists directly to process their items.
